findings.issue: First-publication recovery can remove its pending marker before the private consumption record is durable.
findings.disposition: Recovery re-syncs the exact consumed receipt before finalizing the public artifact set.

findings.issue: Two interrupted first publications can prevent one another from reaching recovery.
findings.disposition: Recover each exact owned journal before requiring complete workspace discovery for another write.

findings.issue: Idle shutdown can strand an advancing Codex child search before source-proven descendants are discovered.
findings.disposition: An advancing bounded search continues across the idle boundary and worker lifetimes.

findings.issue: A consumed receipt can divert a moved ledger or reject an interrupted ordinary refresh at its original home.
findings.disposition: Current canonical resolution takes precedence, and exact owned v2 recovery validates the saved prior ledger.

findings.issue: A receipt retired after observing a portable ledger can strand an interrupted ordinary refresh.
findings.disposition: A closed receipt permits same-inode v2 recovery with an exact valid prior ledger and no fresh first-write authority.

findings.issue: Repeated terminal scans for the same unresolved hints can cause unbounded worker handoffs.
findings.disposition: Completed sweeps stay closed until fresh native evidence or explicit reconciliation warrants a new pass.

findings.issue: The gate can accept a rendered active-duration total that disagrees with native and ledger totals.
findings.disposition: Compare the rendered duration, ledger rollup and independent native measurements.

findings.issue: The native gate can credit later artifacts to a prior publication or miss the actual first completion-aware commit.
findings.disposition: Retain ordered fixture-local diagnostic copies and verify the artifact pair against the earliest eligible commit.

findings.issue: The held ledger snapshot can misclassify completed child time as provisional.
findings.disposition: Check held duration per owner against native completion and active interval evidence at the cutoff.

findings.issue: A missing OpenCode task tool can let the pinned gate pass without its supported grandchild.
findings.disposition: Require exact nested native and ledger parentage for both pinned clients.

findings.issue: The native oracle can overlook duplicate ledger tool rows and a fabricated cache-write field.
findings.disposition: Reject duplicate tool rows and unsupported persisted cache-write fields, and record what the native fixture exposes.

findings.issue: The focused SQLite test does not force a full worker retry after registry contention.
findings.disposition: The test exercises real typed lock classification and review traces the bounded retry. The native timing sample with contention predates the retry change.

findings.issue: Native binding without a conventional type could permanently block first publication.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Native bindings require an explicit type and an incomplete historical binding can complete for the exact ticket.

findings.issue: Conflicting native types stopped refresh before resolving a unique canonical ledger.
findings.disposition: Fixed. The canonical ledger supplies its recorded type and history. A fresh ticket with conflicting types stays pending.

findings.issue: A vanished tentative destination prevented a later verified correction.
findings.disposition: Fixed. A durably unattempted receipt may yield to the new eligible destination. Attempted receipts retain exact recovery.

findings.issue: Title-only conflicts blocked first publication before reconciling either pending root.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Each root retains its accepted metadata and refreshed facts while publication is blocked.

findings.issue: Setup could write a pending path that overlapped effective local private state.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Setup and local updates validate the effective configuration pair before writing.

findings.issue: A tentative native selection could publish despite a later conflicting verified indication.
findings.disposition: Fixed. The ticket and directory leases protect destination revalidation, and registration writes serialize with marker admission.

findings.issue: Promotion could discard the only recorded anomaly evidence for an unavailable owner.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Coverage checks distinguish omitted and recorded-empty or nonempty summaries. A conflict retains both artifacts.

findings.issue: Pending publication could acknowledge a directory entry whose durability was unconfirmed.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Admission syncs the pending leaf and ancestors, including no-op retries after rename or unlink.

findings.issue: A rolled-back marker could reappear after its attempted selection was superseded.
findings.disposition: Fixed. The original directory is synced under its lease after marker and ledger absence are verified.

findings.issue: Focused tests omitted retry after a durable commit with pending cleanup interrupted.
findings.disposition: Fixed. Tests reconstruct that state, verify nonduplicating cleanup and preserve a replacement snapshot observed after the original digest.

findings.issue: The native gate could validate a later corrected ledger instead of the first commit.
findings.disposition: Fixed. The oracle checks the first committed artifact against native facts at its own cutoff, including intervals crossing the cutoff.

findings.issue: Staged path-name comparisons could miss changes to already-staged content.
findings.disposition: Fixed. The native gate compares full Git index entries and blob IDs through promotion.

findings.issue: A temporary native proof failure can detach previously accepted descendants from discard suppression and restore coverage.
findings.disposition: Retain accepted project and parent membership through proof downgrades. Require valid current coverage on restore.

findings.issue: OpenCode can issue a root control invitation before recording a verified link to an unbound parent.
findings.disposition: Persist native parentage and recheck it when accepting control. Preserve controls for independently bound roots.

findings.issue: An idle OpenCode worker can acknowledge a restore wake and retire before bounded descendant discovery finishes.
findings.disposition: Give exact group progress a finite scheduler rotation and carry only the remaining allowance across worker lifetimes.

findings.issue: Restore can wait for an upstream registration outside the admitted independent capture.
findings.disposition: Require reads and discovery within the admitted group and retain its verified native parent link.

findings.issue: A restore can be acknowledged while the published ledger still holds old facts for an owner covered in an earlier pass.

reporters.identity_note: Native tester role observed. Execution model and effort were unavailable.

findings.disposition: Merge the exact operation's accepted snapshots and compare every group member before acknowledging durable materialization.

findings.issue: An OpenCode restore receipt can remain valid when the owner's native history changes without a callback.
findings.disposition: Revalidate the exact native owner checkpoint before reusing a read. A silent native edit requires a new bounded read.

findings.issue: Normal workspace discovery can reject an interrupted ordinary refresh before discard can recover a ledger without a first-publication receipt.
findings.disposition: Validate the exact prior ledger in the retained transaction journal under publication ownership before recovery.

findings.issue: An unrelated same-ticket branch can keep an otherwise covered restore pending.
findings.disposition: Scope native descendant checks and accepted reads to the exact restoring group.

findings.issue: A stale manual reconciliation can overwrite the accepted source snapshot that a newer restore pass used for coverage.
findings.disposition: Fence source and annotation commits by the observed control revision and exact owner observation. Recheck the persisted record before accepting coverage.

findings.issue: An exposed OpenCode binding credential can serve as the signing seed for a control request.
findings.disposition: Use a distinct private seed per worktree and native owner for revision- and action-scoped control credentials.

findings.issue: A legacy worker can lose its leader and leave an automatic child publisher alive before the child has a ticket lease.
findings.disposition: Require a recorded incompatible process group to retire before admitting a compatible worker or control.

findings.issue: Same-ticket siblings can exhaust the restore scheduler's rotation before it reaches the requested group.
findings.disposition: Give restoring owners their own bounded rotation and cursors alongside the ordinary work classes.

findings.issue: A stale OpenCode page can overwrite the cursor reset by restore and skip available descendants.
findings.disposition: Save the OpenCode cursor only when the observed operation revision still matches under the lifecycle lock.

findings.issue: The native gate can sample its canonical baseline after discard has already changed the root or summary.
findings.disposition: Capture exact bytes under the publication directory lock before starting native discard and compare both artifacts through acknowledgement and suppressed work.
